deities: Shiva (as Ladukeswar / Ladu Baba, Shiva linga)

history.dynasty: Original shrine attributed to 9th century CE (Kainchhi/Kainchi temple); present structure by the Ranapur state king Jagdev Ranendra, 19th century CE (CONFLICT: one source dates the present temple to 1942 CE; verify)
history.summary: CAUTION: Wikipedia's 'Ladu Baba Temple' article describes a DIFFERENT 13th-century temple in Bhubaneswar old town (Uttara Daraja, Badu Sahi) - it does not describe this Sarankul shrine, which some web sources conflate. The Sarankul Ladukeswar temple is the famous 'Ladu Baba' of Nayagarh district, where the Shiva linga is worshipped affectionately as Ladukesh Mahesh / Ladu Baba. Legend says a cow daily milked itself over a stone on Bhandar mountain; when the stone bled after being struck by the cow's hoof, a temple was built for the self-manifested linga. The deity is venerated as a compassionate, affectionate form of Shiva, and uniquely, worship has traditionally been conducted by priests of low caste. The temple blends Kalinga and Dravidian architecture and hosts Vaishnava, Shaiva and Sadhu traditions; devotees offer ladu (sweet balls) to the deity.

name: Ladukeswar Temple (Ladubaba)
town_description: Saranakul (also spelled Sarankul or Sharanakula) is a town in Nayagarh district, Odisha, about 13 km from Nayagarh town on the Nayagarh-Aska road. It is best known for the Ladukeswar (Ladu Baba) Shiva temple, one of the most visited pilgrimage centres of the district.
